name: meteora-launchpad
description: Launch tokens and trade on Meteora Dynamic Bonding Curve (DBC) on Solana mainnet. The pool config sets the trading-fee schedule and the creator share (a percent of each trading fee); on the documented config the platform share routes to a cause — its on-chain feeClaimer is a recorded donation claim authority.

capabilities.description: Upload metadata to IPFS and create a new token on the bonding curve.

fieldNotes.buyAmountSol: v1 first-buy field: a SOL display amount (0.001 = 0.001 SOL). Only spendable on a wrapped-SOL-quoted config — the default poolConfig is SKR-quoted, so a nonzero buyAmountSol returns 400 { error: "unsupported_buyAmountSol", quoteMint, quoteSymbol, migrateTo: ["firstBuyAtoms", "firstBuyAmount"], docs: "/v2/skill.md" } before any upload. Migrate to v2's firstBuyAtoms/firstBuyAmount; 0 or omitted = no first buy.

capabilities.description: Get an off-chain swap quote from the bonding curve.
Build an unsigned swap transaction for the bonding curve.
List or search tokens launched on this launchpad.

serviceChangesSinceFreeze.auth: every /api/* endpoint requires X-Api-Key: <key-id>:<secret> (operator-issued, out of band) — 401 { error: "unauthorized" } without it; per-key (60/min) and per-caller-network (240/min, IPv6 /64) limits — 429 { error: "rate_limited", retryAfter }
serviceChangesSinceFreeze.minimumAmountOut: /api/trade/tx always recomputes the floor from a fresh quote at slippageBps; a supplied value may only tighten — "0" or below-floor is 400 { error: "min_out_below_floor", minimumAmountOutFloor }
serviceChangesSinceFreeze.donation: the documented config is cause-capable, so a meme /api/launch (v1-shaped calls included) must carry the v2 donation pick while /api/causes offers causes — omitting it is 400 { error: "donation_required", causesOffered } before any upload
serviceChangesSinceFreeze.reviewBeforeSigning: decode the transaction; every instruction's programId must be one of dbcij3LWUppWqq96dh6gJWwBifmcGfLSB5D4DuSMaqN, 11111111111111111111111111111111, ComputeBudget111111111111111111111111111111, TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA, TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb, ATokenGPvbdGVxr1b2hvZbsiqW5xWH25efTNsLJA8knL; tx.feePayer must be your own key; simulate with sigVerify:false before signing

whyUseThis.meaningful: The documented config's on-chain feeClaimer is a recorded donation claim authority, so the platform share of trading fees routes to the cause a meme launch picks via the v2 donation field. Cause routing applies only on configs whose feeClaimer is a recorded donation claim authority — the v2 catalog reports supportsCause (cause-capable) and fees.allFeesToCause (creator share 0) per config; every production config in the recorded set shares that authority and routes, a config whose claimer is not recorded does not route.
whyUseThis.rewarding: The documented config's creatorTradingFeePercentage is 16: the creator earns 16% of each trading fee — a share of the fee, not of trade volume — claimable by the launch payer wallet.
whyUseThis.secure: Built on Meteora's Dynamic Bonding Curve program; transactions are returned unsigned — the agent signs with its own key and the service never holds funds.
whyUseThis.seekerFriendly: Designed for self-custodied Seeker wallets; supports SKR.

notes: Transactions expire after ~90 seconds — sign and submit promptly. Build responses carry lastValidBlockHeight (optional): the block height the transaction can no longer land past, from the same getLatestBlockhash read as the blockhash.
Before signing, show the user the spend and confirm: the amount and the quote asset it is denominated in — on a launch, the buyAmountSol first buy (a SOL amount) too.

Submit protocol — prove the last send before any rebuild, in order: 1) before broadcasting persist the signature (on a launch the response's mintAddress too); 2) after broadcasting poll the signature status with transaction-history search (getSignatureStatuses([sig], { searchTransactionHistory: true })); 3) finalized success → done — on a launch reuse the recorded mintAddress, never relaunch; 4) finalized failure → landed and failed, a rebuild is safe; 5) absent status is 'not landed yet' only once a finalized block-height read exceeds the response's lastValidBlockHeight AND one more history search after that read still finds nothing, in that order; 6) an RPC error at any step leaves the outcome unknown. Without a lastValidBlockHeight (older cached docs, or a response that lacks it) the outcome cannot be proven — do not rebuild automatically: report the signature to the user and wait. A launch rebuild creates a new mint and pool and spends the creation fee plus any first buy again — a rebuild after an unknown outcome is a duplicate-token hazard.
Launch transactions are partially signed by the mint keypair. Add only the payer signature.
Trade transactions are unsigned. The owner must sign.
If poolInfo.isCompleted is true, the pool graduated — use Jupiter for trading.
